System overview — the components at a glance

The moving parts of a SATOM installation — web console, background services, database, metrics store and the appliances it manages — and how they fit together.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereServer side (systemd units under /etc/systemd/system, application under /opt/satom)
On this page
  • The big picture
  • Components
  • The managed appliances
  • Single node or high-availability pair
  • Where the data lives

The big picture#

A SATOM installation is one Linux server (or a primary + standby pair) running a Flask web application, a handful of small background services, a PostgreSQL database and a metrics store. Operators reach it with a browser; SATOM reaches the appliances over their management APIs and SSH.

Browser ──HTTPS──▶ nginx (TLS) ──▶ gunicorn: SATOM web console
                                       │
                                       ├──▶ PostgreSQL  (inventory, settings, audit, jobs index, SoT index …)
                                       ├──▶ data/ directory (SoT blobs, config-backup vault, runtime files)
                                       ├──▶ metrics store (VictoriaMetrics, local only)
                                       └──▶ appliances: REST / JSON-RPC and SSH
                                              FortiWeb · FortiADC · FortiAuthenticator · FortiAnalyzer

Background services (systemd): scheduler · reconciler · alert engine · Sentinel responder
                               · integration hooks · self-update runner · certificate renewal

If you know the Network Automation Forum's reference framework, the same picture reads as its six building blocks: the templates and baselines are the Intent, the Source of Truth and the metrics store the Observability, the sync, scrape, SNMP and syslog paths the Collector, the writes the Executor, Processes and Change Requests the Orchestrator, and the console and API the Presentation. SATOM is mapped to that framework — see Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

Components#

Component What it does Runs as
Web console The application you use in the browser. Served by gunicorn (4 workers, request timeout 600 s) from the satom.service unit. satom.service
nginx Terminates HTTPS and forwards requests to gunicorn. Port 80 redirects to HTTPS. nginx
Scheduler Fires due scheduled actions (backups, syncs, probe sweeps, approved changes). It only runs on the primary node; on a standby it waits and re-checks every 30 seconds. satom-scheduler.service
Reconciler Runs on both HA nodes. In manual mode it only observes; in automatic mode it drives the staged self-update so the nodes stay on the same code. satom-reconciler.service
Alert engine Checks certificates, devices, Git and backups and pushes findings by email and to the in-app bell. satom-alerts.timer (every 15 minutes)
Sentinel responder Applies, expires and verifies Sentinel responses. satom-responder.timer (every minute)
Integration hooks runner Executes integration hook requests queued by the console. satom-integrations.path (on request)
Self-update runner Performs a software update requested from the console. The web tier only queues the request; this privileged one-shot unit does the work. satom-updater.path (on request)
Node certificate renewal Renews the node's own service certificate when it was issued by a CA. satom-cert-renew.timer (daily at 03:30)
PostgreSQL The management database: users, profiles, appliances, settings, audit log, change requests, scheduled actions, the device configuration cache and the source-of-truth version index. postgresql
Metrics store A single-node VictoriaMetrics instance listening on 127.0.0.1:8428 only, keeping 396 days of samples. Powers Metrics and the monitoring analytics boards. satom-metrics.service
data/ directory Files that do not belong in the database: content-addressed source-of-truth snapshots, the configuration-backup vault, rediscovery snapshots and job ledgers. (files under the application directory)

ℹ️Note

The rate limiter and the shared cache use in-process memory unless a Redis URL is configured (RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI / CACHE_REDIS_URI in .env). Redis is optional; the installer does not install it.

The managed appliances#

SATOM does not install anything on the appliances. Each registered appliance is reached with the address, port and credentials stored on its Appliances entry (the password is stored encrypted):

  • FortiWeb, FortiADC — REST API, plus SSH where the API cannot reach (for example CLI configuration dumps and configuration backups).
  • FortiAuthenticator — REST API.
  • FortiAnalyzer — JSON-RPC API.

Which REST path to call for which firmware is not hard-coded: it is resolved through the endpoint registry (see API registry).

Single node or high-availability pair#

Topology What you get
Standalone One node with a local PostgreSQL.
Primary + standby PostgreSQL streaming replication to the standby, plus a data sync of the data/ directory from the primary. The standby is read-only; the scheduler only fires on the primary. The top bar shows PRIMARY or STANDBY on each node.

See High availability for promotion and failover.

Where the data lives#

  1. 1ApplianceConfiguration read by Rediscovery, Deep capture and scheduled syncs
  2. 2Device cache (PostgreSQL)What most pages render from — fast, works when the box is down
  3. 3Source-of-truth storeVersioned, de-duplicated snapshots: an unchanged config costs no new version
  4. 4Backup vaultConfiguration backups you create or upload, per appliance
  5. 5Metrics storeTime series for health and capacity charts

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the shipped satom.service itself binds gunicorn to 127.0.0.1:8000, so a software update no longer re-opens port 8000 on all addresses; existing nodes receive the new unit at their next update.

Advanced Process and security details
  • The unit templates in deploy/ declare User=root; the installer (and deploy/migrate-deprivilege.sh on existing nodes) adds a systemd drop-in that runs the web console, scheduler and other units under the unprivileged service account.
  • The shipped satom.service binds gunicorn to 127.0.0.1:8000, so the web console is only reachable through nginx, also after a software update.
  • The service account may only run nginx -t and systemctl reload nginx through sudo (used when a node certificate is installed).
  • Secrets live in /opt/satom/.env. FERNET_KEY encrypts the stored appliance passwords and cannot be regenerated — back it up.
  • The metrics store unit is sandboxed (ProtectSystem=strict, write access only to /var/lib/satom-metrics).
  • Full detail: Architecture, Services and timers, Security model, Installation.
